$comment: Authored port of the hand-written registry group iam-groups (docs/plans/compat-coverage-modelgen.md §3.11, #1116). One spec in place of the six per-language implementations of that group (go-sdk, python-sdk, node-js-sdk, cli, java-sdk, dotnet-sdk) — and of the one that was never written: rust-sdk carries 6 rows of parity debt for this group, which the port closes. It soaked as iam-groups-shadow beside those natives until the nightly comparison (run 36216883533) agreed on every one of its 42 (suite, test) pairs in each of three soak runs; the flip then renamed it to iam-groups, pointed the hand-written registry entry at it and deleted the native code. The clauses are the union of what the six natives asserted — see compat/model/README.md § Authored scenarios. No policy document is sent or read back, so there is no `equalsJSON` here.

groups.$comment: One group and one user. The natives split two ways on whose group the tests act on. node-js-sdk and cli create the group's group in the CreateGroup test and delete that same group in DeleteGroup, and java-sdk deletes the group its setup made there — which is what the registry's depends record (every test hangs off CreateGroup). go-sdk, python-sdk, java-sdk and dotnet-sdk create the group's group in setup; go-sdk and dotnet-sdk then have CreateGroup and DeleteGroup each create and remove a throwaway second group, and python-sdk's DeleteGroup does the same, so their DeleteGroup proves the delete of a group nothing else touched. The port takes the first shape: CreateGroup creates the group under `$name` "group" and exports its id, and DeleteGroup deletes it — after RemoveUserFromGroup has emptied it, which it has in declaration order, so AWS has no DeleteConflict to raise. The user is made in setup, as go-sdk, python-sdk, cli and java-sdk do (node-js-sdk and dotnet-sdk create it inside AddUserToGroup, which a scenario test cannot: a test makes one call). IAM is eventually consistent (IAM User Guide, troubleshoot_general.html#troubleshoot_general_eventual-consistency), so every clause that reads a change back through a second call is an `eventually` with the generated iam recipe's budget (6 × 500 ms). No native polls, and Overcast answers on the first attempt. Teardown takes the user out of the group, then deletes the group and then the user, in the order every native teardown does; after a clean run only the user is left, and each teardown call is individually wrapped, so their errors are logged and ignored.
groups.name: iam-groups

tests.$comment: dotnet-sdk asserts Group.GroupId is non-empty and that GetGroup then answers with the name it created (about a throwaway group of its own); python-sdk and java-sdk assert only that setup made the group; go-sdk, node-js-sdk and cli nothing but success. The union: the response names the group and carries a GroupId, and GetGroup, polled, answers with that name and that id. Group.Arn is added: Arn is a required member of the Group shape the response returns (API_Group.html), and this port pins it present, not its account-dependent value. Names: go-sdk oc-grp-<runId>, python-sdk <runId>-group, node-js-sdk <runId>-grp, cli iam-grp-<runId>, java-sdk compat-grp-<runId>, dotnet-sdk <runId>-iam-group; `$name` "group" is the run- and group-scoped spelling.
tests.name: CreateGroup

tests.$comment: No native asserts anything after AddUserToGroup returns; node-js-sdk and dotnet-sdk create the user here first (see the group's $comment). ListGroupsForUser checks the membership from the user's side next; the port asserts the documented effect from the group's side here — GetGroup lists the user among its Users (API_GetGroup.html) — polled.
tests.name: AddUserToGroup

tests.$comment: go-sdk, python-sdk, node-js-sdk, java-sdk and dotnet-sdk assert the group is among the user's Groups, by name; cli nothing but success. The union is that membership, and the port also matches the GroupId CreateGroup returned, which ties the entry to the group this run created rather than to any group of that name.
tests.name: ListGroupsForUser

tests.$comment: No native asserts anything after RemoveUserFromGroup returns. The port asserts the documented effect from both sides, both polled: ListGroupsForUser no longer names the group, and GetGroup no longer lists the user.
tests.name: RemoveUserFromGroup

tests.$comment: All six natives agree: Group.GroupName is the group's name (node-js-sdk and go-sdk also that Group is present, which that implies). The port adds that Group.GroupId is the id CreateGroup returned — a group's unique id is stable for its lifetime (IAM User Guide, reference_identifiers.html#identifiers-unique-ids) — and that Users is a list: it is a required member of the response (API_GetGroup.html). Its contents are not asserted, because GetGroup depends only on CreateGroup and so says nothing about where membership stands; `isList` rather than a presence check, because an absent list and an empty one must read alike in every backend (README § Assertions).
tests.name: GetGroup

tests.$comment: node-js-sdk, cli and java-sdk delete the group's group and assert nothing after; go-sdk and python-sdk create and delete a throwaway group and assert only success; dotnet-sdk does the same and then asserts GetGroup on it raises NoSuchEntity. The port deletes the group's group (see the group's $comment) and asserts dotnet-sdk's claim about it, polled; NoSuchEntity is in GetGroup's modeled errors. depends mirrors registry.json exactly.
tests.name: DeleteGroup
